name: Gerlafingen oxygen converter
summary: In 1948 Robert Durrer's small experimental converter at Gerlafingen, Switzerland, blew oxygen onto molten iron from above, an early trial of oxygen steelmaking.
description: Robert Durrer’s experimental converter applied oxygen from above the iron bath.

links.statement: The 1949 Gerlafingen oxygen-blowing operation used a two-ton Bessemer converter with vertical oxygen blowing.
links.scope: The specific Gerlafingen experimental operation described in the court’s account of the May 1949 Trenkler memo, not every oxygen converter or the exact 1948 configuration.
links.alternatives: Other converter vessels and oxygen-lance arrangements were possible; the cited 1949 operation changed the blowing medium and geometry relative to the conventional bottom-air process.
links.caveats: The primary 1949 memo and original experimental logs were not independently inspected; the court opinion is a later account in a contested patent case. The evidence does not prove the same two-ton vessel was used in every 1948 heat.
links.timing: The older pneumatic process predates the documented 1949 oxygen experiments; this edge identifies a specific equipment connection rather than a complete single-inventor genealogy.

evidence.locator: Section II.C(2), 1949 Trenkler memo discussion, numbered items 1–4
evidence.supports: The court recounts that the May 1949 Gerlafingen operation used a two-ton Bessemer converter and vertical pure-oxygen blowing.
